quizTitle: Fun Facts About TV and Music Streaming

questions.question: Netflix started as a DVD rental service before becoming a streaming giant.
questions.answer: True - Netflix originally mailed DVDs before shifting fully to streaming.

questions.question: Spotify was launched before YouTube.
questions.answer: False - YouTube launched in 2005, Spotify came later in 2008.

questions.question: Binge-watching a TV series was first popularized by streaming services.
questions.answer: True - Streaming platforms encouraged binge-watching by releasing whole seasons at once.

questions.question: Apple Music pays more royalties to artists per stream than Spotify.
questions.answer: True - Apple Music generally pays higher royalties than Spotify.

questions.question: The most-watched streaming event ever was the finale of 'Game of Thrones'.
questions.answer: False - While very popular, the 'Game of Thrones' finale was mainly on HBO, a cable channel; some streaming records are held by other shows.

questions.question: YouTube Premium offers an ad-free music experience similar to Spotify Premium.
questions.answer: True - YouTube Premium allows ad-free videos and background music listening.

questions.question: Streaming platforms use complex algorithms to recommend shows and songs tailored to your taste.
questions.answer: True - Algorithms analyze your viewing/listening habits to suggest content.

questions.question: Most streaming services offer a free subscription tier with no ads.
questions.answer: False - Free tiers often include ads to generate revenue.

questions.question: The term 'streaming' means downloading a file completely before playing it.
questions.answer: False - Streaming plays data in real-time without downloading the entire file first.

questions.question: Podcasts are now commonly available on most music streaming platforms.
questions.answer: True - Platforms like Spotify and Apple Music have large podcast libraries.
